newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Bucharest bourse closes stronger. [CORRECTED 14:20 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Bucharest bourse closes stronger. [CORRECTED 14:20 GMT]

text.p: The Bucharest stock exchange gained further strength on Mondayon increased foreign interest, and the market was seen climbing higher.
"There was fresh foreign money in the market today, with investors buying heavily into first-tier chemical plants and pharmaceuticals companies," a trader said.
"It's something we expect to keep up during this week," he added.

Three independent market indices, the VAB, the BIG and the CAS-SE, based on average prices and market capitalisation, drifted to new highs, rising by 3.8 (corrects from 3.08), 3.67 and 3.79 percent respectively from last Friday.

The average quotes of 22 stocks rose and of 10 slipped. Eleven companies had no trade and two were suspended. Chemical plant Oltchim was briefly halted from trading before issuing a statement on its latest shareholders' meeting.
The statement said Oltchim was planning to raise its capital, issue bonds worth $50 million on international markets and buy new equipment.
Volume swelled to 4.8 million shares from 3.5 million and turnover gained some 5.3 billion lei to 21.1 billion.
There were also two special deals in Azomures fertiliser maker, in 230,000 shares worth 949.5 million lei.
"There was great focus on the first tier, which had some 87 percent of turnover, but buyers also started showing preference for cheap but promising second-tier stocks," said a broker.
On the top tier, five of the eight stocks ended higher and two fell. Refrigerator maker Arctic stayed suspended.
